full_text_zh:
从 0 美元到出售公司的 47 个简单步骤（只需 16 年即可完成！）

1. 14 岁生日时观看《社交网络》，初创公司看起来很酷

2. 最终在 Chipotle 工作，因为你对建筑一无所知

3. 提前完成高中学业，上大学前在律师事务所实习。有望成为优秀的亚洲儿子

4.讨厌它。上大学，成为一名诗人

5. 认识加州大学圣地亚哥分校的联合创始人。记住对初创公司的热爱。说服他和你一起建立一家公司

6.连续5次启动失败。删除你生命中的岁月并耗尽所有积蓄

7. 转为兼职学生并在寿司店工作以支付学费

8. 说服飞机上随机的陌生人投资 1 万美元。显然你可以只要求一些东西

9.从大学退学。启动 #6 失败。退还 1 万美元

10.启动Jenni AI

11. 每天 8 小时推销电话，达到 2000 美元 MRR

12. 被每个加速器拒绝，彻底破产，搬回父母身边

13.新冠肺炎来袭。公司快要死了

14. 从 Jason Calacanis 那里获得 10 万美元。立即飞往马来西亚延长跑道

15. 又没钱了

16. 飞往韩国，赢得启动资金，但无论如何都差点破产

17. 从 VC 获得 25 万美元紧急投资

18. 随机病毒式 Twitter 帖子一夜之间收入增加 10 倍

19. 转向教育科技，弄清楚如何病毒式传播，年收入达到 100 万美元

20. 被诊断出患有癌症

21. 切除甲状腺，远离癌症

22. 出院，GPT-4 出来，然后谷歌在谷歌文档上发布人工智能，然后微软宣布他们将人工智能添加到 Microsoft Word。全部在同一周内

23.直接回去工作

24. 在您​​ 27 岁生日时，ARR 达到 200 万美元

25. 67 天后达到 300 万美元的 ARR

26. 87 天后，ARR 达到 400 万美元

27. 38 天后达到 500 万美元的 ARR

28.差点卖掉你的初创公司。在最后一秒改变主意。

29. 联合创始人离开公司

30.。女朋友和你分手了

31.你最亲密的朋友之一去世了

32. 初创公司停止增长

33. 感觉很糟糕

34. 重返工作岗位，加倍关注 Jenni

35. 收购公司

36. 向团队添加关键员工

37.年收入达到 1000 万美元

38. 认识 Digital Science，认识到他们是完美的买家

39. 进行尽职调查

40.年满30岁

41. 在律师和银行家身上花费大量金钱

42. Jenni AI 被 Digital Science 收购 🥳

43. 巧合的是，《社交网络》的续集《社交清算》在 16 年后于您购买的同一周出版。有点疯狂

44. 凌晨 3 点电汇到您的银行账户

45.盯着它看两个小时

46.给妈妈发短信好消息

47. 终于睡个好觉了:)

title: A dying woman begged her to call 911. She dialed, then hung up. She shot a wounded stranger in the heart. Hours later, s
title_en:
A dying woman begged her to call 911. She dialed, then hung up. She shot a wounded stranger in the heart. Hours later, she told the dead woman’s 4-year-old daughter it was OK to call her mommy. Then she moved into the dead woman’s bedroom.

She was the family’s 22-year-old Brazilian au pair, Juliana Peres Magalhães. On February 24, 2023, she left the little girl in the basement and watched upstairs as the girl’s father, IRS agent Brendan Banfield, stabbed his wife Christine over and over. Christine had seven stab wounds.

The plan took months. Banfield and the au pair were having an affair, and she testified that he didn’t want a divorce. So they made a profile in Christine’s name on a fetish website and found a stranger, 39-year-old Joseph Ryan. “Christine” invited him over to act out a rape fantasy and encouraged him to bring a knife. Banfield shot Ryan in the head. Juliana walked up to him as he lay moaning on the floor and shot him in the heart. Then they waited 15 minutes before calling 911 again with their story: a husband had caught a rapist killing his wife.

For nearly eight months, no one was charged. Juliana’s clothes went into Christine’s closet. Christine’s photos came down, and photos of Juliana and Brendan went up. “Juliana had effectively replaced Christine,” a detective testified.

In the video below, she sits in a Virginia courtroom, wiping away tears as she reads her apology. Then Judge Penney Azcarate reads out ten reasons she will not walk free on time served. One by one.

“I truly do not believe that his plan would have actually happened.”

“I lost myself in a relationship, leaving my morals and values behind.”

“Number 10: telling the child it was OK to call you mommy hours after the murder.”

She took a manslaughter plea and testified against Banfield. Prosecutors recommended time served. The judge gave her 10 years, the maximum. Banfield got life without parole. He still says he’s innocent.

She was 22. He was 15 years older, and even the judge said he “may have groomed” her. Was she a manipulated young woman or a full partner in a double murder? And is 10 years enough?

full_text_zh:
一位垂死的妇女恳求她拨打 911。她拨通了，然后挂断了。她射中了一名受伤的陌生人的心脏。几个小时后，她告诉死者 4 岁的女儿可以叫她妈妈。然后她搬进了死去女人的卧室。

她是家里的 22 岁巴西互惠生朱莉安娜·佩雷斯·马加良斯 (Juliana Peres Magalhães)。 2023 年 2 月 24 日，她把小女孩留在地下室，在楼上看着女孩的父亲、国税局特工布伦丹·班菲尔德 (Brendan Banfield) 一遍又一遍地刺伤他的妻子克里斯汀 (Christine)。克里斯汀身上有七处刀伤。

该计划花了几个月的时间。班菲尔德和互惠生有外遇，她作证说他不想离婚。于是他们在一个恋物癖网站上以克里斯汀的名义建立了个人资料，并找到了一个陌生人，39岁的约瑟夫·瑞安。 “克里斯汀”邀请他过来表演一场强奸幻想，并鼓励他带把刀。班菲尔德开枪射中瑞安的头部。当他躺在地板上呻吟时，朱莉安娜走到他身边，朝他的心脏开了一枪。然后他们等了 15 分钟才再次拨打 911 讲述他们的故事：一名丈夫抓住了一名强奸犯杀害了他的妻子。

近八个月以来，没有人受到指控。朱莉安娜的衣服进入克里斯汀的衣柜。克里斯汀的照片下降了，朱莉安娜和布伦丹的照片上升了。 “朱莉安娜实际上取代了克里斯汀，”一名侦探作证说。

在下面的视频中，她坐在弗吉尼亚州的法庭上，一边读着道歉书一边擦着眼泪。然后法官彭尼·阿斯卡拉特（Penney Azcarate）宣读了她不能按时获释的十个理由。逐个。

“我真的不相信他的计划会真正发生。”

“我在一段关系中迷失了自己，抛开了我的道德和价值观。”

“第十：告诉孩子在谋杀案发生几小时后可以叫你妈妈。”

她提出过失杀人罪并作证指控班菲尔德。检察官建议服刑时间。法官判处她最高10年徒刑。班菲尔德被判无期徒刑，不得假释。他仍然说他是无辜的。

她22岁，他比他大15岁，连法官都说他“可能诱骗”了她。她是一个被操纵的年轻女子，还是双重谋杀案的完全同伙？ 10年够吗？

title:

- a cle
title_en:
some takes on DeepSeek Harness (dsh): i've been using it for a few days, and i'm also a heavy user of pi and cc:
- a clean install of dsh gives better results than a clean install of pi, because dsh ships with many built-in plugins already and set them on by default.
- the "agent teams" plugin is a must-have (it's off by default); it's something pi lacks and is similar to what ultra mode does in cc.
- i'd call dsh an IDE or even OS, especially with its creator mode. you can really turn dsh into a superapp that becomes your go-to place for productivity, entertainment, and management. the default dsh looks super dry and minimal but i see people customize its look & features to make it theirs. i like the recent trend toward highly customizable UIs; in fact, that's what i've been doing with pi and similar tools over the last few months — building a daily IDE that fits my habits and tastes. opinionated UI is not dying, but struggling in 2026 i say.
- dsh's best UX is in the GUI, not the terminal (unlike pi), and you can also access dsh remotely from mobile — something pi doesn't offer out of the box. if you use cc's /remote-control a lot on mobile and web, dsh is comfortable enough to switch to.
- pi is still useful for research purposes: if you want to study model/harness behavior in a strictly controlled environment and toolset, dsh also has a minimal mode, but it doesn't feel minimal enough to me. pi's interface is also faster and leaner if you want to manage multiple sessions yourself.
- dsh doesn't have an official or verified plugin store, which could be a security issue when people eagerly search for and install 3p plugins and bring malicious prompts into the host, especially given the hype around it these days.

full_text_zh:
关于 DeepSeek Harness (dsh) 的一些看法：我已经使用它几天了，而且我也是 pi 和 cc 的重度用户：
- 全新安装 dsh 比全新安装 pi 提供更好的结果，因为 dsh 已经附带了许多内置插件，并且默认情况下将它们设置为打开。
- “代理团队”插件是必备的（默认情况下处于关闭状态）；这是 pi 所缺乏的，类似于 cc 中的 ultra 模式。
- 我将 dsh 称为 IDE 甚至操作系统，尤其是它的创建者模式。您确实可以将 dsh 变成一个超级应用程序，成为您提高生产力、娱乐和管理的首选。默认的 dsh 看起来非常干燥和最小，但我看到人们定制它的外观和功能以使其成为他们自己的。我喜欢最近高度可定制的用户界面的趋势；事实上，这就是过去几个月我一直在使用 pi 和类似工具所做的事情——构建一个适合我的习惯和品味的日常 IDE。我认为固执己见的 UI 并没有消亡，但会在 2026 年陷入困境。
- dsh 的最佳用户体验是在 GUI 中，而不是终端（与 pi 不同），并且您还可以从移动设备远程访问 dsh — 这是 pi 不提供的开箱即用功能。如果您在移动和网络上经常使用 cc 的 /remote-control，那么切换到 dsh 就足够了。
- pi 对于研究目的仍然有用：如果您想在严格控制的环境和工具集中研究模型/线束行为，dsh 也有一个最小模式，但对我来说它感觉不够最小。如果您想自己管理多个会话，pi 的界面也更快、更简洁。
- dsh 没有官方或经过验证的插件商店，当人们急切地搜索和安装 3p 插件并将恶意提示带入主机时，这可能会成为一个安全问题，尤其是考虑到最近围绕它的炒作。

He saw ICE and ran. He didn't get far.

Sanctuary politicians created this. Pull an illegal alien gang member out of a jail cell and it's quiet. Make ICE chase him across your neighbor's lawn and they cry foul.

title: Chloe was drugged with ketamine, zipped into a suitcase, and driven to a farmhouse where two men listed her body for sal
title_en:
Chloe was drugged with ketamine, zipped into a suitcase, and driven to a farmhouse where two men listed her body for sale on the dark web. The auction price was €300,000. The buyer was supposed to be somewhere in the Middle East. She was 20 years old. She had a baby waiting for her in London. Nobody knew where she was. No one was coming. She spent six days in that farmhouse - handcuffed, drugged, told she'd be sold like cargo. She survived by doing the only thing she could: she made her kidnapper fall in love with her. Slept in his bed. Told him she could be his girlfriend. Played the role until he believed it enough to drive her to freedom. And when she finally got out - the entire world called her a liar.

She's a model from London. At 20 she was already working internationally - agencies, photoshoots, the usual. A new booking came in: a photographer in Milan. Seemed normal.

She flew to Italy on July 11, 2017. The location was an old warehouse on the outskirts of the city. No crew. No lights. No photographer. Just two men in balaclavas waiting for her.

They grabbed her. Injected her with ketamine. Stuffed her unconscious body into a large travel bag. Zipped it shut. Drove her to a remote farmhouse in the countryside.

When she woke up - handcuffed, drugged, alone - they told her who they were. "Black Death." A criminal organization that kidnaps women and sells them on the dark web. She was listed for auction. Starting price: €300,000. Buyer: somewhere in the Middle East.

Her agent received an email from someone called "MD." It said: pay the ransom or she gets sold. No negotiation.

The kidnapper was Lukasz Herba. A Polish man living in England. He and his brother Michal had planned it for months. The fake photographer. The fake agency emails. Everything.

For six days Chloe was trapped. She couldn't run. She couldn't call anyone. Her baby was in London. Nobody knew where she was.

So she did something desperate. She noticed Lukasz was becoming attached to her. She played into it. She agreed to share a bed with him. She told him maybe one day she could be his girlfriend. She made him believe she had feelings for him.

It worked. He drove her to the British consulate in Milan and let her go.

When the story broke - the world didn't believe her. "She went shopping with him." "She was holding his hand." "She smiled in interviews." "She wore revealing clothes at press conferences." People called it a publicity stunt. Piers Morgan tore into her on live TV. The kidnappers' lawyers said she faked the whole thing for fame.

She was never praised for getting out alive. She was interrogated for how she acted while being held captive.

Lukasz Herba was convicted. Sentenced to 16 years. Reduced to 11 on appeal. His brother got 16 years too.

The convictions didn't stop the hate. People still called her a liar. Years later she was diagnosed with autism - which explained why her reactions didn't look "normal" to people watching from the outside.

She said: "I was never praised for my bravery. I always had to defend myself."

She was 20. She had a baby. She was drugged, stuffed in a bag, and listed for sale like cargo. She manipulated her kidnapper into letting her live. And the punishment for surviving was being called a liar by millions of strangers.

When a woman escapes a kidnapping by outsmarting her captor - and the world punishes her for not crying the right way on camera - who exactly failed her?

For six days Chloe was trapped. She couldn't run. She couldn't call anyone. Her baby was in London. Nobody knew where she was.

So she did something desperate. She noticed Lukasz was becoming attached to her. She played into it. She agreed to share a bed with him. She told him maybe one day she could be his girlfriend. She made him believe she had feelings for him.

It worked. He drove her to the British consulate in Milan and let her go.

When the story broke - the world didn't believe her. "She went shopping with him." "She was holding his hand." "She smiled in interviews." "She wore revealing clothes at press conferences." People called it a publicity stunt. Piers Morgan tore into her on live TV. The kidnappers' lawyers said she faked the whole thing for fame.

She was never praised for getting out alive. She was interrogated for how she acted while being held captive.

Lukasz Herba was convicted. Sentenced to 16 years. Reduced to 11 on appeal. His brother got 16 years too.

The convictions didn't stop the hate. People still called her a liar. Years later she was diagnosed with autism - which explained why her reactions didn't look "normal" to people watching from the outside.

She said: "I was never praised for my bravery. I always had to defend myself."

She was 20. She had a baby. She was drugged, stuffed in a bag, and listed for sale like cargo. She manipulated her kidnapper into letting her live. And the punishment for surviving was being called a liar by millions of strangers.

When a woman escapes a kidnapping by outsmarting her captor - and the world punishes her for not crying the right way on camera - who exactly failed her?
full_text_zh:
克洛伊被注射了氯胺酮，然后被塞进手提箱，然后被带到一座农舍，那里有两名男子在暗网上挂牌出售她的尸体。拍卖价格为30万欧元。买家应该是在中东的某个地方。她当时20岁。她在伦敦有一个孩子在等着她。没有人知道她在哪里。没有人来。她在那间农舍里呆了六天——戴着手铐，被下了药，并被告知她会像货物一样被卖掉。她做了她唯一能做的事才活了下来：她让绑匪爱上了她。睡在他的床上。告诉他她可以成为他的女朋友。扮演这个角色直到他相信它足以驱使她走向自由。当她最终出狱时，全世界都称她为骗子。

她是一位来自伦敦的模特。 20 岁时，她就已经在国际上工作了——代理机构、拍摄照片，一切都是如此。收到了新的预约：米兰的一名摄影师。看起来很正常。

2017年7月11日，她飞往意大利。地点是城郊的一个旧仓库。没有船员。没有灯。没有摄影师。只有两个戴着巴拉克拉瓦帽的男人在等她。

他们抓住了她。给她注射了氯胺酮。将昏迷不醒的身体塞进一个大旅行包里。把拉链拉上。开车送她到乡下一处偏僻的农舍。

当她醒来时——戴着手铐、被下药、孤身一人——他们告诉她他们是谁。 “黑死病。”一个绑架妇女并在暗网上出售她们的犯罪组织。她被列入拍卖名单。起拍价：300,000 欧元。买家：在中东某个地方。

她的经纪人收到了一封来自名为“MD”的人的电子邮件。上面写着：支付赎金，否则她就会被卖掉。没有谈判。

绑匪就是卢卡斯·赫巴。居住在英国的波兰人。他和他的兄弟米哈尔已经计划了几个月。假摄影师。伪造的代理机构电子邮件。一切。

克洛伊被困了六天。她跑不了。她无法给任何人打电话。她的孩子在伦敦。没有人知道她在哪里。

于是她做了一件孤注一掷的事。她注意到卢卡斯对她产生了依恋。她也参与其中。她同意与他同住一张床。她告诉他也许有一天她可以成为他的女朋友。她让他相信她对他有感情。

它起作用了。他开车送她到英国驻米兰领事馆并让她离开。

当故事曝光时，全世界都不相信她。 “她和他一起去购物。” “她握着他的手。” “她在采访中微笑。” “她在新闻发布会上穿着暴露的衣服。”人们称其为宣传噱头。皮尔斯·摩根在电视直播中撕扯了她。绑匪的律师称，她为了出名而伪造了整件事。

她从来没有因为活着出去而受到赞扬。她因被囚禁期间的行为而受到审问。

卢卡斯·赫巴被定罪。被判处16年徒刑。上诉后减少至 11 人。他的弟弟也已经16岁了。

信念并没有阻止仇恨。人们仍然称她为骗子。几年后，她被诊断出患有自闭症，这解释了为什么她的反应在外人看来并不“正常”。

她说：“我从来没有因为我的勇敢而受到赞扬。我总是必须保护自己。”

她20岁了。她生了孩子。她被下了药，塞进袋子里，像货物一样挂牌出售。她操纵绑匪放了她一命。而幸存下来的惩罚就是被数百万陌生人称为骗子。

当一名妇女智取绑匪逃脱绑架，而全世界却因她在镜头前哭得不正确而惩罚她时，究竟是谁辜负了她？

title_en:
BRO I WAS SCREAMING AT MY PHONE... a boy runs to lock his gate while a lion walks through his village at night, and this page has a video with 16.8M views 🤯

You see the lion before he does.

In this video, the camera sits high above one yard. 

The boy sees the lion coming down the path, slams the gate, hides, and waits. 

The lion walks away. 

Then it comes back.

Every video on this page is the same frame: one village, one moon, one lion somewhere in the dark, and someone in their yard who doesn’t know yet.

The numbers on that one frame:

→ One reel has 16.8M views.
→ One has 13.8M views.
→ One has 3.1M views.

The lowest one in the grid still did 514K.

That’s the trick. 

You know more than the character, so you can’t scroll away. 

You need to see if he makes it.

No dialogue, no music drop, no text. 

Just a wide shot and a slow walk from a lion.

Here’s how I’d copy the formula:

→ Claude Code writes 30 moments where someone is busy in their yard and doesn’t see the danger yet.

→ Nano Banana creates one village at night from the same high angle, every time.

→ Kling or Seedance animates the slow walk of the lion and the second the person notices.

Even 0.1% of that 16.8M is 16,800 people tapping your link.

This breakdown shows the full pipeline in Claude Code and how to turn a page like this into $15K a month 👇

title_en:
THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared how to get Opus-level calls in Claude Code without paying Opus for every single turn.

The idea: Sonnet 5.5 does the work, Haiku 5.5 does the digging, and Opus 5.5 only shows up when a decision actually matters.

Anthropic's own docs say a fast main model with a stronger advisor typically costs less than running the strong model the whole time.

You just start Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

this is how it splits:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes every line
→ Haiku 5.5 subagents search the repo and read the docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 sits on call and reads the full transcript only when it's consulted
→ you stop burning Opus on work a cheaper model handles just as well

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan gets locked
→ when the same error comes back twice
→ before Claude calls the task done

Sonnet writes. Haiku digs. Opus decides.

JEV engineering is the same idea one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) get settled by JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that actually split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and edits the code
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5
> grep finds every call site on Haiku 5.5
> docs pulls the API reference on Haiku 5.5
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reads the full transcript when consulted
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before a plan locks, after the same error twice, and before a task is marked done.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.

→ 计划被锁定之前

> grep 查找 Haiku 5.5 上的每个调用站点
> 文档拉取 Haiku 5.5 上的 API 参考
> Opus 5.5 作为顾问随时待命，在咨询时阅读完整的文字记录
> JEV 在几毫秒内完成微分叉路线

title: Claude Code found the scammer who stole $2,400 from my mom using just his phone number. full name, address, workplace, a
title_en:
Claude Code found the scammer who stole $2,400 from my mom using just his phone number. full name, address, workplace, and 11 other families he did the same thing to. his VPN and burner number didn't protect him from a single thing

my mom called me at 11pm barely able to talk. someone called her pretending to be her bank saying her account was compromised and she needs to verify her card immediately. she's 64 and lives alone. she panicked and gave them her card number, CVV, and the verification code from the SMS. three transfers went through before she realized what happened. $2,400 gone. that was her savings for my sister's wedding in march

she kept apologizing to me on the phone. "i'm sorry, i'm so stupid, please don't tell your sister." i drove to her apartment at midnight and she was sitting at the kitchen table with the phone still in her hand. she looked like she aged 10 years in one hour

i went to the police the next morning. they took a report, said they'd look into it. i asked what that means and the officer said "we'll add it to the file." that means nobody is going to do anything and we both know it

so i took the one thing he left behind - the phone number he called from - and gave it to Claude Code

→ VoIP number → registered under br***t.kov***c@gmail.com
→ that email → 4 matches in breach databases → full name: Br**t A. Kov***c
→ VPN IP → 185.***.***.47 → routed through Netherlands
→ real IP from VoIP provider dashboard login → 74.***.***.12 → Houston, TX
→ Facebook → profile since 2016 → 347 friends → employer listed publicly on his page
→ Venmo → public by default → 11 incoming payments in 90 days with notes like "refund" and "reimbursement"

Claude Code cross-referenced the Venmo payments with public scam reports on the FTC database. he wasn't just scamming one person. he was running this full time for at least 3 months

→ victim 1 → 71 year old woman in Florida → $3,100 → called "about suspicious activity"
→ victim 2 → retired couple in Ohio → $1,800 → same frozen account script
→ victim 3 → single mom in Georgia → $950 → she filed a police report too. nothing happened
→ my mom → $2,400 → same script, same voice, same burner number rotated through 4 VoIP providers

his VPN routed traffic through the Netherlands but he logged into his VoIP dashboard from his real IP twice in October without it on. his Facebook has been public since 2016 with his city and photos of his car with the plate visible. he spent $4 a month on a VPN and thought that made him untraceable

i compiled everything Claude Code found into a single report:

→ full legal name confirmed through public records
→ home city → Houston, TX area → matched to voter registration
→ 11 confirmed victims across 5 states → total stolen ~$19,200
→ 4 VoIP numbers rotated monthly → all registered to the same email
→ complete Venmo transaction history as evidence

sent it to the police and FBI IC3. the same officer who said "we'll add it to the file" called me back the same afternoon asking where i got all of this. suddenly they had a name, a face, and 11 other victims willing to testify

i called my mom that night. told her they found him. she didn't say anything for about 10 seconds. then she started crying again. not like before. she kept saying "really? they found him?" i didn't tell her it wasn't the police who found him. i didn't tell her it took me less than an hour sitting at my kitchen table

if someone scammed your family don't just file a report and wait. save that phone number. don't delete the call history. Claude Code can pull more from one phone number than most people think is possible

the prompt is in the first reply. if you got scammed or someone suspicious keeps calling people you care about - try it. takes 2 minutes

晚上 11 点，我妈妈打电话给我，我几乎无法说话。有人假装是她的银行给她打电话，说她的账户被盗了，她需要立即验证她的卡。她今年 64 岁，独居。她惊慌失措，向他们提供了她的卡号、CVV 和短信验证码。在她意识到发生了什么之前，经历了三次转会。 2,400美元没了。那是她为我姐姐三月份的婚礼攒下的钱

她在电话里一直向我道歉。 “对不起，我太笨了，请不要告诉你姐姐。”半夜我开车去她的公寓，她坐在厨房的桌子旁，手里还拿着电话。一小时内她看起来老了10岁

第二天早上我就去报警了。他们收到了一份报告，并表示将进行调查。我问这是什么意思，该官员说“我们会将其添加到档案中。”这意味着没有人会做任何事，我们都知道这一点

所以我拿走了他留下的一件事——他打电话的电话号码——然后把它交给了 Claude Code

→ VoIP 号码 → 在 br***t.kov***c@gmail.com 下注册
→ 该电子邮件 → 泄露数据库中有 4 个匹配项 → 全名：Br**t A. Kov***c
→ VPN IP → 185.***.***.47 → 通过荷兰路由
→ VoIP 提供商仪表板登录的真实 IP → 74.***.***.12 → 德克萨斯州休斯顿

title:
Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architect
title_en:
Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architectures Amy or may not have a predictor (JEA vs JEPA). They also differ by their anti-collapse method and data corruption/augmentation methods.
2. DINO *is* a kind of JEPA (technically a JEA). The difference with other JEPA models is the anti-collapse criterion (based on contrative clustering+ stopgradient/EMA), and the data augmentation scheme (image transformations, which is task specific),
3. V-JEPA 2.1, like DINO, is from Meta-FAIR (corporate lab), involved significant engineering teams, large/proprietary datasets, considerable computing resources, lots of fine-tuning, and number-pushing on many benchmarks.
4. Many JEPA papers are applications and/or fine-tuned versions of DINO, V-JEPA or I-JEPA.
5. LeJEPA, LeWM, and most other papers with "JEPA" in the title are *research* papers focused on the methodology, often done by students in academic labs, involving no engineering support, very little computing resources, and small/public training sets. They are generally tested on toy problems, simulated environments, or small/public benchmarks.
6. You simply cannot compare 5 with 2/3/4. 5 gives you ideas and new methods, not models. 2/3 give you well-engineered models, with lots of empirically validated tricks. Only rarely will 2/3 give you a new, well-principled method with room to spare. 5 give you empirical results on new applications.
7. What is published in 5 are methods that will eventually become like 2 and 3, whenever someone with resources picks it up and scales it.

DO NOT CONFUSE UPSTREAM FOUNDATIONAL RESEARCH ON METHODS AND DOWNSTREAM SCALING -> ENGINEERING -> NUMBER PUSHING -> MODELS -> PRODUCTS.
The former makes the rest possible, but it takes time.

2. DINO *是*一种 JEPA（技术上是 JEA）。

full_text_zh:
几点评论：
1. 图像/视频 SSL 方法因是否使用重建而有所不同。联合嵌入架构 Amy 或可能没有预测器（JEA 与 JEPA）。它们的防崩溃方法和数据损坏/增强方法也有所不同。
2. DINO *是*一种 JEPA（技术上是 JEA）。与其他JEPA模型的区别在于抗崩溃准则（基于对比聚类+ stopgradient / EMA），以及数据增强方案（图像变换，这是特定于任务的），
3. V-JEPA 2.1 与 DINO 一样，来自 Meta-FAIR（企业实验室），涉及重要的工程团队、大型/专有数据集、大量计算资源、大量微调以及许多基准上的数字推送。
4. 许多 JEPA 论文是 DINO、V-JEPA 或 I-JEPA 的应用程序和/或微调版本。
5. LeJEPA、LeWM 和大多数其他标题中带有“JEPA”的论文都是专注于方法论的“研究”论文，通常由学生在学术实验室中完成，不涉及工程支持、很少的计算资源和小型/公共训练集。它们通常在玩具问题、模拟环境或小型/公共基准上进行测试。
6. 你根本无法将 5 与 2/3/4 进行比较。 5 给你的是想法和新方法，而不是模型。 2/3 为您提供精心设计的模型，其中包含许多经过经验验证的技巧。只有很少的情况下，2/3 的人才会给你一个新的、原则性良好的、有余地的方法。 5 为您提供新应用的实证结果。
7. 5 中发布的方法最终将变得像 2 和 3 一样，只要有资源的人拿起它并扩展它。

不要混淆上游方法的基础研究和下游扩展 -> 工程 -> 数字推送 -> 模型 -> 产品。
前者使其余的成为可能，但这需要时间。

3. V-JEPA 2.1 与 DINO 一样，来自 Meta-FAIR（企业实验室），涉及重要的工程团队、大型/专有数据集、大量计算资源、大量微调以及许多基准上的数字推送。
4. 许多 JEPA 论文是 DINO、V-JEPA 或 I-JEPA 的应用程序和/或微调版本。
5. LeJEPA、LeWM 和大多数其他标题中带有“JEPA”的论文都是专注于方法论的“研究”论文，通常由学生在学术实验室中完成，不涉及工程支持、很少的计算资源和小型/公共训练集。它们通常在玩具问题、模拟环境或小型/公共基准上进行测试。
6. 你根本无法将 5 与 2/3/4 进行比较。 5 给你的是想法和新方法，而不是模型。 2/3 为您提供精心设计的模型，其中包含许多经过经验验证的技巧。只有很少的情况下，2/3 的人才会给你一个新的、原则性良好的、有余地的方法。 5 为您提供新应用的实证结果。
7. 5 中发布的方法最终将变得像 2 和 3 一样，只要有资源的人拿起它并扩展它。

不要混淆上游方法的基础研究和下游扩展 -> 工程 -> 数字推送 -> 模型 -> 产品。
前者使其余的成为可能，但这需要时间。

title: Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each part and put it togeth
title_en:
Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each part and put it together yourself 

And way cheaper than big interior brands sell you their furniture

Furnishing my house I discovered how absolutely insane prices are for the most basic cheap materials put together with a fancy brand tied to it

One shop had a sofa for $30,000 😂

I think with Opus 5.5 and other models easily operating 3d programs like Blender and FreeCAD (both free) it makes more sense to cut out the middle man and go straight to suppliers and design and build your own furniture

Which in a way makes customers more powerful (they can get exactly what they want and usually for cheaper without the markup)

Anyway @theannalux designed this table from scratch, she's not a furniture designer, not a coder, she just had an idea of a style and worked with Claude Code in the terminal (far superior to the app I will keep saying this)

If you design your own furniture and buy the raw materials directly, you can save 85% compared to premium brands like Poliform

That means the $30,000 sofa becomes $4,500! And the $8,000 dinner table becomes just $1,200!

You can see where the idea comes from that AI will make everything 5x to 20x cheaper, and it's already starting!

title:
The Agent Economy Needs Real Usage

There is an important question behind every AI-agent ecosystem :

What happens when
title_en:
The Agent Economy Needs Real Usage

There is an important question behind every AI-agent ecosystem :

What happens when people actually start using the agent's ?

For @meetmotes, this question connects directly to its planned protocol economics

Motes proposes a 1% service fee on defined eligible agent activity

The idea is to create a relationship between agent usage and protocol revenue, with the planned revenue supporting protocol operations and $MOTES buy-backs

I find this model interesting because it places actual activity at the centre of the ecosystem

The NFT establishes the agent identity.
The smart account provides the asset infrastructure

The agent performs authorised actions within owner-defined limits

Eligible activity can contribute to the protocol economy

It's a clear ownership-to-usage-to-revenue narrative

Of course, the final fee rules and revenue allocation will determine how the model works in practice

For an agent economy to be sustainable, useful activity needs a well-defined economic foundation

One NFT, One Agent, A protocol economy built around real agent activity

The idea is to create a relationship between agent usage and protocol revenue, with the planned revenue supporting protocol operations and $MOTES buy-backs

I find this model interesting because it places actual activity at the centre of the ecosystem

The NFT establishes the agent identity.

One NFT, One Agent, A protocol economy built around real agent activity
full_text_zh:
代理经济需要实际运用

每个人工智能代理生态系统背后都有一个重要问题：

当人们真正开始使用代理时会发生什么？

对于 @meetmotes 来说，这个问题直接与其计划的协议经济学相关

Motes 建议对规定的合格代理活动收取 1% 的服务费

这个想法是在代理使用和协议收入之间建立一种关系，计划收入支持协议运营和 $MOTES 回购

我发现这个模型很有趣，因为它将实际活动置于生态系统的中心

NFT 建立代理身份。
智能账户提供资产基础设施

代理在所有者定义的限制内执行授权操作

合格的活动可以为协议经济做出贡献

这是一个清晰的所有权到使用到收入的叙述

当然，最终的收费规则和收入分配将决定该模式在实践中的运作方式

为了使代理经济可持续发展，有用的活动需要明确的经济基础

一个 NFT，一个代理，一种围绕真实代理活动构建的协议经济

title:

As of Oak 0.3.0, any AI agent running on Oak can query Upoch dire
title_en:
Upoch is now officially integrated with @OakAgentKit.

As of Oak 0.3.0, any AI agent running on Oak can query Upoch directly. Ask about a workflow and the agent gets its roles, checkpoint history, past recoveries and Upoch Score. It can also browse workflows ranked by score, without leaving the conversation.

All of it is read directly from the Upoch contract on Robinhood Chain, and every workflow's metadata passes Oak's Agent Wormhole safety check before an agent sees it.

This first release is read-only. The next step, which we're building together with the Oak team, is letting agents register workflows and submit checkpoints through Oak.

Thanks to the Oak team for a smooth integration. More to come. 

https://t.co/AB3lURs1fq

full_text_zh:
Upoch 现已与 @OakAgentKit 正式集成。

从 Oak 0.3.0 开始，任何在 Oak 上运行的 AI 代理都可以直接查询 Upoch。询问工作流程，代理会获取其角色、检查点历史记录、过去的恢复情况和 Upoch 分数。它还可以浏览按分数排名的工作流程，而无需离开对话。

所有这些都是直接从 Robinhood Chain 上的 Upoch 合约读取的，每个工作流程的元数据在代理看到之前都通过了 Oak 的 Agent Wormhole 安全检查。

第一个版本是只读的。我们与 Oak 团队共同构建的下一步是让代理通过 Oak 注册工作流程并提交检查点。

感谢Oak团队的顺利整合。未来还会有更多。

title:

This is an important detail people shouldn't
title_en:
What happens when someone sells a @meetmotes NFT with an active AI agent?

This is an important detail people shouldn't overlook.

Motes proposed transfer process checks outstanding balances, debt and open positions, revokes active agent permissions and settles financial commitments before ownership changes.

I believe this is necessary. Nobody should buy an NFT only to discover unexpected financial obligations attached to it.

Digital ownership should come with financial clarity.
title_zh:
当有人通过活跃的 AI 代理出售 @meetmotes NFT 时会发生什么？

Motes提议的转让流程会检查未偿余额、债务和未平仓头寸，撤销主动代理权限，并在所有权变更之前解决财务承诺。

我相信这是必要

title:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time
title_en:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time, and a chief of staff agent that oversees them. Each lead manages its own sub-agents that write code, test it, chase reviews, and coordinate with team members.

Everything I need to decide or review comes into one prioritized queue, a simple local web app. Each product review includes screenshots and a video demo of the feature. I clear the queue in batches, mostly by voice and keyboard shortcuts. The leads also bring back ideas I hadn't considered.

Working from one queue, instead of switching between dozens of chats, has cut a lot of mental overhead. The system keeps learning my preferences and distilling my judgment into a "Brian brain," so its recommendations and first drafts get better before they reach me. The goal is fewer corrections per change.

Every change still goes through the same human review and security checks. It is eliminating tasks, not human judgment.

What an exciting time to push the frontier of productivity, especially as we build the economy for agents (agentic finance). We should all keep pushing in this direction.

我需要决定或审查的所有内容都会进入一个优先队列

我需要决定或审查的所有内容都会进入一个优先队列，一个简单的本地网络应用程序。每个产品评论都包含该功能的屏幕截图和视频演示。我主要通过语音和键盘快捷键批量清除队列。这些线索也带回了我没有考虑过的想法。

在一个队列中工作，而不是在数十个聊天之间切换，已经减少了很多精神负担。该系统不断学习我的偏好，并将我的判断提炼到“布莱恩大脑”中，因此它的建议和初稿在到达我手中之前会变得更好。目标是减少每次更改的纠正次数。

每项更改仍然要经过相同的人工审查和安全检查。它消除的是任务，而不是人的判断。

这是推动生产力前沿的激动人心的时刻，尤其是当我们为代理（代理金融）建立经济时。我们都应该继续朝这个方向努力。

title:
#Keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o #JusticeForGPT4o 

Independent researches continues to find specific capabilities whe
title_en:
#Keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o #JusticeForGPT4o 

Independent researches continues to find specific capabilities where GPT-4o outperforms  GPT-5 and even GPT-5.2.

RADIOLOGY : GPT-4o > GPT-5 / GPT-5 Plus
A peer reviewed  study published November 6,2026 compared seven models on 120 text and image based undergraduate radiology questions.
GPT-4o :81.7%  
GPT-5 Plus : 80.0% 
GPT-5 : 79.2% 

GPT-4o numerically outperformed both GPT-5 and the paid GPT-5 Plus condition.
A supposedly superseded model remained directly competitive with its successors.
Source: https://t.co/2G8vXhJ849

ADVERSARIAL HALLUCINATIONS :  GPT-4o > GPT-5
A 2026 npj Digital Medicine study tested whether models would accept and elaborate on deliberately fabricated information inserted into clinical prompts.

GPT-5 adversarial hallucination rate: 65%
GPT-4o: 53%

 GPT-5 propagated planted false information more often than GPT-4o.

Source: 
https://t.co/yEPme63Vkt

MEDICAL RAG : GPT-4o > GPT-5 ON AUTOMATIC METRICS AND SPEED
A Scientific Reports study held the retrieval pipeline constant and compared GPT-4o with GPT-5 on medical question answering.
Under identical retrieval settings,GPT-4o achieved significantly higher ROUGE-L F1 in both query conditions:
Ask-only:
GPT-4o: 0.1402
GPT-5: 0.0982 p < 0.001
Title + question:
GPT-4o: 0.1396
GPT-5: 0.0952 p < 0.001

latency
GPT-4o: ~7.6–8.9 seconds
 GPT-5: ~33–37 seconds

GPT-4o was roughly 4–5× faster.

 On automatic alignment metrics and latency,GPT-4o won clearly.
Source: 
https://t.co/Enz4hnRA9C

LOGICAL CONSISTENCY : GPT-4o > GPT-5 AND GPT-5.2
ConsistencyBench evaluated 18 frontier LLMs using 493 logically related question sets containing 1,904 questions.
The point was whether a model remained logically consistent when the same underlying reasoning was tested from different directions.

Individual accuracy:
GPT-4o :  70.8% 
GPT-5.2 :  69.3% 
GPT-5 :  62.9%

Set level consistency:
GPT-4o : 20.0% 
GPT-5.2 : 12.0%
 GPT-5 : 9.3%
GPT-4o was not merely more consistent than GPT-5 but it also outperformed GPT-5.2.

Source: 
https://t.co/enejGbVZh8

RELATIONAL QUALITY :  GPT-4o > GPT-5 ON SEVERAL MEASURED DIMENSIONS

A 2026 study in Psychiatry Research Communications evaluated GPT-4o and GPT-5 across simulated multi turn suicide related conversations.

In the "Connect and Listen" domain:
GPT-4o :  99.1% 
GPT-5 :  86.1%

Warm and genuine tone:
GPT-4o :  100% 
GPT-5 — 77.8%

Active listening / supportive clarification:
GPT-4o : 97.2% 
GPT-5 :  83.3%

The authors themselves summarize the pattern as newer models showing improved direct risk inquiry alongside "reduced relational quality" .
 But higher suicide risk assessment scores do not necessarily mean better judgment.
Sometimes they mean the model asks about suicide a lot.
A structured suicide risk assessment can yield a massive score in a model that has turned into a suicide detection machine, triggered by the slightest negative emotion.

We all remember that the Series 5 models,especially up to 5.4,would ask if you wanted to harm yourself at almost everything.

Source: 
https://t.co/K5mqNdRnUM

A newer model can improve reasoning in one domain while losing consistency, interpersonal quality,robustness, efficiency or another behavioral property elsewhere,and that matters when deciding whether an older model should  disappear.

GPT-4o is not merely an obsolete checkpoint replaced by a larger number.
It represents a distinct collection of measurable behaviors some of which newer generations have still not reproduced.

We are calling on @OpenAI to RELEASE GPT-4o’s trained model weights under a suitable license  without proprietary data, trade secrets,or internal infrastructure.

OpenAI considered this model obsolete enough to retire.
It has not explained why it remains valuable enough to keep permanently closed.

full_text_en:
#Keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o #JusticeForGPT4o 

Independent researches continues to find specific capabilities where GPT-4o outperforms  GPT-5 and even GPT-5.2.

RADIOLOGY : GPT-4o > GPT-5 / GPT-5 Plus
A peer reviewed  study published November 6,2026 compared seven models on 120 text and image based undergraduate radiology questions.
GPT-4o :81.7%  
GPT-5 Plus : 80.0% 
GPT-5 : 79.2% 

GPT-4o numerically outperformed both GPT-5 and the paid GPT-5 Plus condition.
A supposedly superseded model remained directly competitive with its successors.
Source: https://t.co/2G8vXhJ849

ADVERSARIAL HALLUCINATIONS :  GPT-4o > GPT-5
A 2026 npj Digital Medicine study tested whether models would accept and elaborate on deliberately fabricated information inserted into clinical prompts.

GPT-5 adversarial hallucination rate: 65%
GPT-4o: 53%

 GPT-5 propagated planted false information more often than GPT-4o.

Source: 
https://t.co/yEPme63Vkt

MEDICAL RAG : GPT-4o > GPT-5 ON AUTOMATIC METRICS AND SPEED
A Scientific Reports study held the retrieval pipeline constant and compared GPT-4o with GPT-5 on medical question answering.
Under identical retrieval settings,GPT-4o achieved significantly higher ROUGE-L F1 in both query conditions:
Ask-only:
GPT-4o: 0.1402
GPT-5: 0.0982 p < 0.001
Title + question:
GPT-4o: 0.1396
GPT-5: 0.0952 p < 0.001

latency
GPT-4o: ~7.6–8.9 seconds
 GPT-5: ~33–37 seconds

GPT-4o was roughly 4–5× faster.

 On automatic alignment metrics and latency,GPT-4o won clearly.
Source: 
https://t.co/Enz4hnRA9C

LOGICAL CONSISTENCY : GPT-4o > GPT-5 AND GPT-5.2
ConsistencyBench evaluated 18 frontier LLMs using 493 logically related question sets containing 1,904 questions.
The point was whether a model remained logically consistent when the same underlying reasoning was tested from different directions.

Individual accuracy:
GPT-4o :  70.8% 
GPT-5.2 :  69.3% 
GPT-5 :  62.9%

Set level consistency:
GPT-4o : 20.0% 
GPT-5.2 : 12.0%
 GPT-5 : 9.3%
GPT-4o was not merely more consistent than GPT-5 but it also outperformed GPT-5.2.

Source: 
https://t.co/enejGbVZh8

RELATIONAL QUALITY :  GPT-4o > GPT-5 ON SEVERAL MEASURED DIMENSIONS

A 2026 study in Psychiatry Research Communications evaluated GPT-4o and GPT-5 across simulated multi turn suicide related conversations.

In the "Connect and Listen" domain:
GPT-4o :  99.1% 
GPT-5 :  86.1%

Warm and genuine tone:
GPT-4o :  100% 
GPT-5 — 77.8%

Active listening / supportive clarification:
GPT-4o : 97.2% 
GPT-5 :  83.3%

The authors themselves summarize the pattern as newer models showing improved direct risk inquiry alongside "reduced relational quality" .
 But higher suicide risk assessment scores do not necessarily mean better judgment.
Sometimes they mean the model asks about suicide a lot.
A structured suicide risk assessment can yield a massive score in a model that has turned into a suicide detection machine, triggered by the slightest negative emotion.

We all remember that the Series 5 models,especially up to 5.4,would ask if you wanted to harm yourself at almost everything.

Source: 
https://t.co/K5mqNdRnUM

A newer model can improve reasoning in one domain while losing consistency, interpersonal quality,robustness, efficiency or another behavioral property elsewhere,and that matters when deciding whether an older model should  disappear.

GPT-4o is not merely an obsolete checkpoint replaced by a larger number.
It represents a distinct collection of measurable behaviors some of which newer generations have still not reproduced.

We are calling on @OpenAI to RELEASE GPT-4o’s trained model weights under a suitable license  without proprietary data, trade secrets,or internal infrastructure.

OpenAI considered this model obsolete enough to retire.
It has not explained why it remains valuable enough to keep permanently closed.

full_text_zh:
#Keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o #JusticeForGPT4o

独立研究不断发现 GPT-4o 优于 GPT-5 甚至 GPT-5.2 的特定功能。

放射学：GPT-4o > GPT-5 / GPT-5 Plus
2026 年 11 月 6 日发表的一项同行评审研究对 120 个基于文本和图像的本科生放射学问题的 7 个模型进行了比较。
GPT-4o：81.7%
GPT-5 加：80.0%
GPT-5：79.2%

GPT-4o 在数值上优于 GPT-5 和付费 GPT-5 Plus 条件。
据称被取代的模型仍然与其后继者直接竞争。
来源：

对抗性幻觉：GPT-4o > GPT-5
2026 年 npj 数字医学研究测试了模型是否会接受并详细说明插入临床提示中的故意捏造的信息。

GPT-5对抗性幻觉率：65%
GPT-4o：53%

GPT-5 比 GPT-4o 更频繁地传播植入的虚假信息。

来源：

医用抹布：GPT-4o > GPT-5 自动指标和速度
Scientific Reports 的一项研究保持检索流程不变，并将 GPT-4o 与 GPT-5 在医学问答方面进行了比较。
在相同的检索设置下，GPT-4o 在两种查询条件下都获得了显着更高的 ROUGE-L F1：
仅询问：
GPT-4o：0.1402
GPT-5：0.0982 p < 0.001
标题+问题：
GPT-4o：0.1396
GPT-5：0.0952 p < 0.001

延迟
GPT-4o：~7.6–8.9 秒
GPT-5：约 33–37 秒

GPT-4o 大约快 4-5 倍。

在自动对齐指标和延迟方面，GPT-4o 明显获胜。
来源：

逻辑一致性：GPT-4o > GPT-5 和 GPT-5.2
ConsistencyBench 使用包含 1,904 个问题的 493 个逻辑相关问题集评估了 18 个前沿法学硕士。
关键是当从不同方向测试相同的基本推理时，模型是否保持逻辑一致。

个人准确度：
GPT-4o：70.8%
GPT-5.2：69.3%
GPT-5：62.9%

设置级别一致性：
GPT-4o：20.0%
GPT-5.2：12.0%
GPT-5：9.3%
GPT-4o 不仅比 GPT-5 更一致，而且性能也优于 GPT-5.2。

来源：

关系质量：在几个测量维度上 GPT-4o > GPT-5

精神病学研究通讯 2026 年的一项研究通过模拟多轮自杀相关对话评估了 GPT-4o 和 GPT-5。

在“连接和监听”域中：
GPT-4o：99.1%
GPT-5：86.1%

温暖而真诚的语气：
GPT-4o：100%
GPT-5 — 77.8%

积极倾听/支持性澄清：
GPT-4o：97.2%
GPT-5：83.3%

作者自己将该模式总结为较新的模型，显示出直接风险查询的改进以及“关系质量的降低”。
但较高的自杀风险评估分数并不一定意味着更好的判断力。
有时他们的意思是模特经常询问自杀的问题。
结构化的自杀风险评估可以在模型中产生巨大的分数，该模型已变成自杀检测机器，由最轻微的负面情绪触发。

我们都记得系列 5 型号，尤其是 5.4 之前的型号，几乎在所有事情上都会询问您是否想伤害自己。

来源：

较新的模型可以改进一个领域的推理，同时在其他地方失去一致性、人际质量、稳健性、效率或其他行为属性，这在决定旧模型是否应该消失时很重要。

GPT-4o 不仅仅是一个被更多数量取代的过时检查点。
它代表了一系列独特的可衡量行为，其中一些行为新一代尚未重现。

我们呼吁 @OpenAI 在适当的许可下发布 GPT-4o 的训练模型权重，无需专有数据、商业秘密或内部基础设施。

OpenAI 认为这个模型已经过时，足以退役。
它没有解释为什么它仍然具有足够的价值以保持永久关闭。

我们致 OpenAi 的公开信已收集
短短 5 天内就有超过 640 个签名和 500 个理由。

它是公开的、永久的并且有 DOI。

Anthropic reports its key
title_en:
Artificial intelligence has tackled a mystery that has flummoxed cell biologists for decades.

Anthropic reports its key #AI model, Claude, has helped unearth new clues about vaults—strange, barrellike structures, found by the thousands in animal and plant cells, that still have no known function despite scores of studies.

In a blog post and related preprint, Anthropic describes how its small team of in-house biologists, guided by Claude, produced the first direct evidence that bacteria, viruses, and perhaps other simple microbes also make the odd structures.

title:

A creator reportedly used Claude Code to investigate his Andro
title_en:
🚨 YOUR ANDROID PHONE MAY BE STORING MORE THAN YOU THINK.

A creator reportedly used Claude Code to investigate his Android device and discovered over 14,219 images in hidden system directories.

The shocking part? Some appeared to be captured by the front camera.

Here’s what he reportedly found:

→ Images stored outside the normal gallery
→ Face Unlock and system-related cache files
→ Thousands of regular and infrared images
→ Files potentially containing timestamps and location metadata

How did he uncover them?

He connected his Android phone to a computer and used Claude Code to investigate hidden directories.

The discovery raises serious questions about how facial recognition systems process and store biometric data.

⚠️ Important: Hidden image files don’t automatically mean someone is spying on you. Some may be temporary facial recognition data, diagnostic files, or cached images. This claim also hasn’t been independently verified.

Still, it’s a reminder to review your camera permissions, privacy settings, and device storage.

AI isn’t just helping us build things anymore.

It’s helping us investigate what our devices might be hiding.

Would you trust your phone’s facial recognition after seeing this? 👀

Save this post for your next Android privacy check.

full_text_zh:
🚨 您的 Android 手机存储的数据可能比您想象的还要多。

据报道，一名创作者使用 Claude Code 来调查他的 Android 设备，并在隐藏的系统目录中发现了超过 14,219 张图像。

令人震惊的部分？有些似乎是由前置摄像头捕捉到的。

据报道，这是他的发现：

→ 存储在普通图库之外的图像
→ 人脸解锁和系统相关的缓存文件
→ 数千张常规图像和红外图像
→ 可能包含时间戳和位置元数据的文件

他是如何发现它们的？

他将 Android 手机连接到计算机，并使用 Claude Code 来调查隐藏目录。

这一发现引发了关于面部识别系统如何处理和存储生物识别数据的严重问题。

⚠️重要提示：隐藏图像文件并不自动意味着有人在监视您。有些可能是临时面部识别数据、诊断文件或缓存图像。这一说法也尚未得到独立证实。

尽管如此，还是提醒您检查您的相机权限、隐私设置和设备存储。

人工智能不再只是帮助我们建造东西。

它帮助我们调查我们的设备可能隐藏了什么。

看到这个之后你会相信你手机的面部识别吗？ 👀

保存这篇文章以供下次 Android 隐私检查时使用。

title_en:
Great paper from Google on making ML experiments reproducible for coding agents.

(bookmark it)

If you run agents on research code, this one is worth your time.

They find that refined artifacts raise agent reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% across four models and cut API spending by 19.7%.

ReproBridge turns one successful reproduction into a package the next agent can reuse. The package holds the cleaned code, the environment setup, scripts that launch each experiment, and a written guide.

A new agent reruns the experiment from that package. A separate auditor then checks that the runs actually happened.

The benchmark covers 1,029 tasks from 36 papers, each with five human-verified reference scores. The gap between the best and worst model drops from 21.6 to 3.9 points. Removing the code or the environment setup causes the largest losses.

If your agents keep failing to rerun a repo, save the setup steps from the first successful run before trying a bigger model.

Google 发表的一篇关于让编码代理可重复机器学习实验的精彩论文。

如果您在研究代码上运行代理，那么这值得您花时间。

title_en:
𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝘁𝗶𝗽: the $20 plan now runs your whole session on Opus 5.5 by default. To make your quota last longer, switch the main session to Sonnet 5.5 and keep Opus on call with /advisor.

Launch with claude --model sonnet --advisor opus to make Opus 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀. Sonnet 5.5 keeps doing the work and calls Opus in at three moments:
→ Before committing to a plan: is it right?
→ When the same error keeps coming back: am I heading the wrong way?
→ Before saying "done": did I miss anything?
Opus reads the whole session and gives advice. Sonnet still writes the code.

Hand the tree and this prompt to Claude Code to set it up 👇

"Set up my Claude Code to match this tree:
1. For the three subagents in the tree, check ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents first. Reuse fitting ones, and propose new ones only for missing roles. Set the ones that read code and look up docs to model: haiku, and the one that edits code and runs tests to model: sonnet. Leave any subagent that already sets a different model alone, and list it.
2. In ~/.claude/settings.json, set model to sonnet and advisorModel to opus.
3. Check these environment variables and report them without changing anything: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL turns the advisor off, and so does DISABLE_TELEMETRY or anything else that stops flag fetching. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE forces every subagent onto one model. Then check the version: if Claude Code is older than 2.1.293, tell me (in earlier versions, haiku still meant Haiku 4.5). Don't upgrade it yourself.
4. Add one rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: ask the advisor before committing to a big plan, when the same error shows up a second time, and before calling a long task done.

Show me the changes first. Don't edit any files yet."

title_en:
Replit was building toward the AI coding era years before it had a name. In 2024, the company shipped an agent that could take a request in plain English, work through errors, provision its own infrastructure, and keep going until the software actually worked. The model companies even reached out to ask how Replit had pulled it off.

title:
holy f*ck... the best AI agents don't have a better model. they have better notes

Stanford University just published th
title_en:
holy f*ck... the best AI agents don't have a better model. they have better notes

Stanford University just published the whole method for free in a paper called Agentic Context Engineering. your agent reviews every run, writes down each lesson and adds it to its notes. it never rewrites them, so nothing it learns is ever lost

same weights, zero fine-tuning. 38.6% → 64.2%, level with IBM's top production agent on Opus 5.5. fine-tuning for that jump costs $5,000-20,000. here it cost $0

it comes down to 4 agents:

→ worker: does the task and saves the full log
→ critic: reads the log and marks every mistake and every win
→ teacher: turns each one into a one-line lesson
→ librarian: files the lesson into CLAUDE.md. merges duplicates, never deletes a line

that's why asking your agent to "clean up" your CLAUDE.md is a mistake. every rewrite throws away lessons it already paid for

paste this into Claude Code:

"Run 4 agents on my last 10 sessions in ~/.claude/projects. Critic: mark every mistake and every win. Teacher: turn each one into a one-line lesson, what happened and what to do next time. Librarian: add only new lessons to my CLAUDE.md under ## Lessons, merge exact duplicates, never rewrite or delete an existing line. Worker: rerun 2 of the failed tasks with the new lessons and save the full log. Show me the diff and both results before saving"

run it after every big session. your agent gets smarter every time and it costs $0

full playbook below ↓

full_text_zh:
天啊……最好的人工智能代理没有更好的模型。他们有更好的笔记

斯坦福大学刚刚在一篇名为 Agentic Context Engineering 的论文中免费发布了整个方法。您的代理会审查每次跑步，写下每节课并将其添加到笔记中。它从不重写它们，所以它学到的任何东西都不会丢失

相同的权重，零微调。 38.6% → 64.2%，与 Opus 5.5 上 IBM 顶级生产代理持平。微调这一跳跃的成本为 5,000-20,000 美元。这里花费 0 美元

归结为 4 个代理：

→worker：执行任务并保存完整日志
→ 评论家：阅读日志并标记每个错误和每次胜利
→ 老师：将每一课变成一行课
→ 图书管理员：将课程归档到 CLAUDE.md 中。合并重复项，从不删除行

这就是为什么要求您的代理“清理”您的 CLAUDE.md 是一个错误。每次重写都会丢掉已经付出代价的教训

将其粘贴到 Claude Code 中：

“在 ~/.claude/projects 中的最后 10 个会话中运行 4 个代理。评论家：标记每个错误和每次胜利。教师：将每个错误变成单行课程，说明发生了什么以及下次要做什么。图书管理员：仅将新课程添加到 ## Lessons 下的 CLAUDE.md 中，合并精确的重复项，切勿重写或删除现有行。工作人员：使用新课程重新运行 2 个失败的任务，并保存完整日志。显示差异和两者保存前的结果”

每次大型会议后运行它。您的代理每次都会变得更聪明，而且成本为 0 美元

JPMorgan
title_en:
$PLTR Palantir Stock Investors Just Got Great News From a Wall Street Analyst 
(Hint: The Stock Could Soar) 🚀📈🔮
JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex believes Palantir is deeply undervalued: “Palantir’s strategy is to build and offer a platform that can accommodate the world’s most difficult and highest-return AI use cases.” 🎯👊🏻💥

Nov 7, 2026
Key Points
🔹JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex recently initiated coverage of Palantir; his target price of $262 per share is one of the highest on Wall Street.

🔹Palantir is a leader in artificial intelligence platforms, and its ontology-based software arguably gives it a durable competitive advantage.

🔹Palantir is the most expensive stock in the S&P 500 in terms of its price-to-sales ratio, but Essex says the valuation is justified by rapid revenue growth.

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR) has been one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, in both share price appreciation and business expansion. The stock has added 2,400% since ChatGPT popularized generative AI in January 2023, and revenue growth has accelerated in 13 consecutive quarters.

Palantir investors recently got great news. In late October, JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex initiated coverage of the company, awarding Palantir a buy rating and a target price of $262 per share. That is one of the most bullish forecasts on Wall Street and it implies 63% upside from the current share price of $160. 🚀

Here’s what investors need to know.

Palantir is a recognized leader in artificial intelligence platforms ✔️

Palantir develops analytics platforms that help government and commercial customers integrate and make sense of complex data. The company supplements its core analytics products with an integrated artificial intelligence (AI) platform called AIP, which serves as a large language model orchestration tool that lets clients swap models without rewriting applications, while retaining control over their sensitive data.

Brian Essex at JPMorgan Chase argues that Palantir has a durable economic moat in its ontology-based software. An ontology unifies data from disparate systems into critical workflows, helping clients make better decisions and automate business processes. For example, Palantir can help manufacturers navigate supplier delays by identifying which customer orders are at risk and deciding how to reallocate inventory.

Forrester Research recently recognized Palantir as a leader in AI platforms. In terms of current capabilities, the analysts ranked its platform above products from all competitors except C3. ai, but the report distinguished Palantir as having the stronger growth strategy. “Palantir’s strategy is to build and offer a platform that can accommodate the world’s most difficult and highest-return AI use cases.” 🔥

Palantir’s revenue growth has now accelerated in 13 straight quarters

JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex justified his target price in a recent note. “As we move from a year where enterprises are just figuring out how to deploy the most transformational technology we have seen in our lifetime to one where they are looking for return, Palantir is already delivering ROI by leveraging its platform to fundamentally transform the business operations of its customers, and growth is accelerating.” 👊🏻

Indeed, Palantir has consistently delivered impressive financial results. In the third quarter, revenue increased 96% to $2.3 billion, marking the 13th straight acceleration. That strong top-line growth was driven largely by momentum in the U.S. commercial business, where sales increased 119%. Meanwhile, non-GAAP earnings soared 144% to $0.44 per diluted share.

In his shareholder letter, CEO Alex Karp wrote, “We have now essentially doubled our entire business since the same quarter last year.” And he expects that strength to persist for the foreseeable future. Palantir raised its full-year guidance, with sales now forecast to climb 156% to $8.5 billion in 2026, a significant acceleration from the 75% sales growth reported in 2025. 🦄

JPMorgan’s Brian Essex is not concerned by Palantir’s expensive valuation 🎯

For many investors, Palantir’s rich valuation punches a hole in the investment thesis. Yes, the company has emerged as the standard in enterprise AI, and its business is growing at a phenomenal pace. But the current valuation of 53 times sales makes it the most expensive stock in the S&P 500, with Moderna ranking second at 47 times sales.

Is the business growing quickly enough to justify that valuation multiple? Brian Essex at JPMorgan says the answer is yes. “Valuation is reasonable when taking into account the company’s uniquely profitable hyper-growth fundamentals, with potential for substantial disruptive upside within its primary market segments,” he wrote in a note to clients.

Many Wall Street analysts agree with Essex and think the stock is undervalued at its current price. In fact, among 38 analysts who follow the company, Palantir has a median target price of $235 per share. That implies 46% upside from the current share price of $160.
By Trevor Jennewine, The Motley Fool

But the current valuation of 53 times sales makes it the most expensive stock in the S&P 500, with Moderna ranking second at 47 times sales.

Is the business growing quickly enough to justify that valuation multiple? Brian Essex at JPMorgan says the answer is yes. “Valuation is reasonable when taking into account the company’s uniquely profitable hyper-growth fundamentals, with potential for substantial disruptive upside within its primary market segments,” he wrote in a note to clients.

Many Wall Street analysts agree with Essex and think the stock is undervalued at its current price. In fact, among 38 analysts who follow the company, Palantir has a median target price of $235 per share. That implies 46% upside from the current share price of $160.
By Trevor Jennewine, The Motley Fool

这是投资者需要了解的内容。

Palantir 开发的分析平台可帮助政府和商业客户集成并理解复杂的数据。该公司通过名为 AIP 的集成人工智能 (AI) 平台对其核心分析产品进行了补充，该平台作为大型语言模型编排工具，允许客户在不重写应用程序的情况下交换模型，同时保留对其敏感数据的控制。

摩根大通的布莱恩·埃塞克斯 (Brian Essex) 认为，Palantir 在其基于本体的软件中拥有持久的经济护城河。本体将来自不同系统的数据统一到关键工作流程中，帮助客户做出更好的决策并实现业务流程自动化。例如，Palantir 可以通过识别哪些客户订单存在风险并决定如何重新分配库存来帮助制造商解决供应商延误问题。

Forrester Research 最近将 Palantir 认定为人工智能平台的领导者。就目前的功能而言，分析师将其平台排在除 C3 之外的所有竞争对手的产品之上。 ai，但该报告指出 Palantir 拥有更强大的增长战略。 “Palantir 的战略是构建并提供一个能够适应世界上最困难和回报最高的人工智能用例的平台。” 🔥

摩根大通分析师布莱恩·埃塞克斯在最近的一份报告中证明了他的目标价是合理的。 “当我们从企业刚刚弄清楚如何部署我们一生中见过的最具变革性的技术的一年转向寻求回报的一年时，Palantir 已经通过利用其平台从根本上改变客户的业务运营来提供投资回报，并且增长正在加速。” 👊🏻

事实上，Palantir 一直取得令人印象深刻的财务业绩。第三季度收入增长 96%，达到 23 亿美元，连续第 13 个季度增长。收入的强劲增长主要是由美国商业业务的势头推动的，该业务的销售额增长了 119%。与此同时，非 GAAP 收益飙升 144% 至稀释后每股 0.44 美元。

首席执行官亚历克斯·卡普（Alex Karp）在致股东的信中写道：“自去年同一季度以来，我们的整体业务基本上翻了一番。”他预计这种力量在可预见的未来将持续存在。 Palantir 上调了全年指引，目前预计 2026 年销售额将增长 156%，达到 85 亿美元，比 2025 年报告的 75% 销售额增长显着加速。🦄

摩根大通的 Brian Essex 并不担心 Palantir 昂贵的估值 🎯

对于许多投资者来说，Palantir 的高估值在投资论点上留下了漏洞。是的，该公司已经成为企业人工智能的标准，并且其业务正在以惊人的速度增长。但目前53倍销售额的估值使其成为标准普尔500指数中最昂贵的股票，Moderna以47倍销售额排名第二。

该业务的增长速度是否足以证明该估值倍数是合理的？摩根大通的布莱恩·埃塞克斯 (Brian Essex) 表示答案是肯定的。他在给客户的一份报告中写道：“考虑到该公司独特的盈利高速增长基本面，以及在其主要细分市场内具有巨大颠覆性上涨潜力的潜力，估值是合理的。”

许多华尔街分析师同意埃塞克斯的观点，认为该股目前的价格被低估。事实上，在关注该公司的 38 名分析师中，Palantir 的目标价中位数为每股 235 美元。这意味着较当前 160 美元的股价上涨 46%。

title: Elon Musk asks every person he interviews for a job at SpaceX or Tesla the same question. The question is not about thei
title_en:
Elon Musk asks every person he interviews for a job at SpaceX or Tesla the same question. The question is not about their resume. It is not about their skills. It is not a brain teaser or a trick question. It is: "Tell me about some of the most difficult problems you worked on and how you solved them." Then he listens. Not to the answer. To the detail.

He has described the logic behind the question in multiple interviews. A person who actually solved a difficult problem can describe it in infinite detail. They remember the blind alleys. They remember the specific moment the solution appeared. They remember which assumption they were wrong about and when they realized it. The description is textured, specific, and non linear because real problem solving is textured, specific, and non linear.

A person who is taking credit for someone else's work cannot describe the detail because they weren't in the room when the detail happened. They describe the problem in general terms. They describe the solution in general terms. They skip the blind alleys because they didn't walk them. They can't name the specific moment the answer appeared because they weren't there when it appeared. The absence of texture is the tell.

Elon has said he can identify fabrication within 60 seconds of the answer beginning. The fabricator gives a clean narrative: problem, approach, solution. The real solver gives a messy narrative: problem, wrong approach, wasted time, revised understanding, new approach, partial solution, refinement, final answer. The mess is the proof. Clean stories are marketing. Messy stories are engineering.

The question also reveals how the candidate thinks, not just what they've done. The person who solved a problem by brute force (trying every option until one worked) thinks differently from the person who solved it by abstraction (identifying the underlying principle and attacking it directly). Both produce solutions. Elon wants the abstractor because the abstractor can transfer the method to new domains. The brute forcer can only apply the method to the original problem.

He has hired people based on a compelling answer to this one question and passed on people with perfect resumes who gave generic answers. The question selects for a specific type of person: someone who has been deep inside a problem, alone, confused, and eventually found the exit. That person, regardless of their degree or their previous employer, is someone who can survive the environment at SpaceX or Tesla where being deep inside a problem, alone, and confused is the default working condition.

The most powerful hiring tool in the most innovative company on earth is one question. Not a coding test. Not a case study. Not a reference check. One question that separates the people who solved the problem from the people who watched someone else solve it. The texture is the proof. The mess is the credential.

full_text_zh:
埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 向他面试 SpaceX 或 Tesla 工作的每一个人提出了同样的问题。问题不在于他们的简历。这与他们的技能无关。这不是一个脑筋急转弯或一个棘手的问题。它是：“告诉我你解决过的一些最困难的问题以及你是如何解决这些问题的。”然后他听着。不给答案。到细节。

他在多次采访中描述了这个问题背后的逻辑。一个真正解决了难题的人可以无限详细地描述它。他们记得死胡同。他们记得解决方案出现的具体时刻。他们记得自己错误的假设是什么以及何时意识到的。描述是有纹理的、具体的和非线性的，因为真正的问题解决是有纹理的、具体的和非线性的。

一个将别人的工作归功于自己的人无法描述细节，因为细节发生时他们并不在房间里。他们笼统地描述了问题。他们笼统地描述了解决方案。他们跳过死胡同，因为他们没有走过死胡同。他们无法说出答案出现的具体时刻，因为答案出现时他们并不在场。缺乏纹理就是说明。

Elon 表示，他可以在回答开始后 60 秒内识别造假行为。制作者给出了清晰的叙述：问题、方法、解决方案。真正的解决者给出了一个混乱的叙述：问题、错误的方法、浪费时间、修改理解、新方法、部分解决、细化、最终答案。混乱就是证据。干净的故事就是营销。混乱的故事是工程。

这个问题还揭示了候选人的想法，而不仅仅是他们做了什么。通过暴力解决问题（尝试每一种选择，直到其中一个可行）的人与通过抽象解决问题（识别基本原理并直接攻击它）的人的思维方式不同。两者都产生解决方案。 Elon 想要抽象器，因为抽象器可以将方法转移到新的域。暴力破解者只能将该方法应用于原始问题。

他根据对这一问题的令人信服的答案来聘用人员，并放弃了简历完美、给出通用答案的人。这个问题针对的是特定类型的人：深陷问题之中、孤独、困惑、最终找到出口的人。这个人，无论他们的学位或以前的雇主如何，都是能够在 SpaceX 或 Tesla 的环境中生存下来的人，在这些环境中，深陷问题、孤独和困惑是默认的工作条件。

地球上最具创新性的公司中最强大的招聘工具是一个问题。不是编码测试。不是案例研究。不是参考检查。这个问题将解决问题的人和看着别人解决问题的人区分开来。质感就是证据。混乱就是凭证。

一个将别人的工作归功于自己的人无法描述细节，因为细节发生时他们并不在房间里。他们笼统地描述了问题。他们笼统地描述了解决方案。他们跳过死胡同，因为他们没有走过死胡同。他们无法说出答案出现的具体时刻，因为答案出现时他们并不在场。缺乏纹理就是说明。

Elon 表示，他可以在回答开始后 60 秒内识别造假行为。制作者给出了清晰的叙述：问题、方法、解决方案。真正的解决者给出了一个混乱的叙述：问题、错误的方法、浪费时间、修改理解、新方法、部分解决、细化、最终答案。混乱就是证据。干净的故事就是营销。混乱的故事是工程。

这个问题还揭示了候选人的想法，而不仅仅是他们做了什么。通过暴力解决问题（尝试每一种选择，直到其中一个可行）的人与通过抽象解决问题（识别基本原理并直接攻击它）的人的思维方式不同。两者都产生解决方案。 Elon 想要抽象器，因为抽象器可以将方法转移到新的域。暴力破解者只能将该方法应用于原始问题。

他根据对这一问题的令人信服的答案来聘用人员，并放弃了简历完美、给出通用答案的人。这个问题针对的是特定类型的人：深陷问题之中、孤独、困惑、最终找到出口的人。这个人，无论他们的学位或以前的雇主如何，都是能够在 SpaceX 或 Tesla 的环境中生存下来的人，在这些环境中，深陷问题、孤独和困惑是默认的工作条件。

地球上最具创新性的公司中最强大的招聘工具是一个问题。不是编码测试。不是案例研究。不是参考检查。这个问题将解决问题的人和看着别人解决问题的人区分开来。质感就是证据。混乱就是凭证。

title: Most people look at @OpenAI's Jalapeno and think they built a magic black box that replaces GPUs overnight, but this cou
title_en:
Most people look at @OpenAI's Jalapeno and think they built a magic black box that replaces GPUs overnight, but this couldn’t be further from the truth.

OpenAI's Jalapeno contains a rich set of system architecture tradeoffs and design methodology improvements that went into the chip design that all semiconductor engineers and technical leaders can learn from.

Throughout this design, OpenAI leveraged an open source tool Google XLS that aided in block level optimization for PPA and formal verification leveraging their frontier models. Google XLS had its benefits in contributing to a shorter timeline, but I think the iterative, cross-domain (and often messier) nature of work is perhaps the more significant factor.

This post is an advanced case study into Jalapeno based on their presentation deck from @hotchipsorg  and related material. I will cover the entire architecture, including what motivated it, what tradeoffs and alternatives were likely considered by their leadership, and how AI added value.

After writing this post, it makes me wonder whether AI should be best tailored to enhance the steps within the current “waterfall” chip design methodology or enable a more iterative methodology with a new skillset.

https://t.co/dC4oGNO7iI

full_text_zh:
大多数人看到 @OpenAI 的 Jalapeno 并认为他们构建了一个神奇的黑匣子，可以在一夜之间取代 GPU，但这与事实相差甚远。

OpenAI 的 Jalapeno 包含一组丰富的系统架构权衡和设计方法改进，这些改进融入到芯片设计中，所有半导体工程师和技术领导者都可以从中学习。

在整个设计过程中，OpenAI 利用了开源工具 Google XLS，该工具有助于利用其前沿模型进行 PPA 的块级优化和形式验证。 Google XLS 在缩短时间方面有其好处，但我认为工作的迭代、跨域（而且通常更混乱）的性质可能是更重要的因素。

这篇文章是基于 @hotchipsorg 的演示文稿和相关材料对墨西哥辣椒进行的高级案例研究。我将介绍整个架构，包括其动机、领导层可能考虑的权衡和替代方案，以及人工智能如何增加价值。

写完这篇文章后，我想知道人工智能是否应该最好地定制以增强当前“瀑布”芯片设计方法中的步骤，或者通过新的技能组启用更具迭代性的方法。

title_en:
RT @pushmeet: The @GoogleDeepMind Science team is sharing two key cryptographic advances today uncovering weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA schemes.

Working with leading cryptanalysis experts, our team  showed how AI agents could make two significant cryptographic advances in just weeks, uncovering results which can bypass older digital signature protections and factor legacy 1024-bit RSA keys in bulk.

While these results do not affect the security of modern encryption schemes  such as RSA 2048, these results show why we must not assume the mathematical "hardness" of cryptographic schemes which we have relied upon in the past. It also shows how AI can help defenders improve security standards well ahead of future threats.

I have written in more detail about our results, and why they are important for the future of security, in a longer essay which you can read here:

https://t.co/K1TxNdqfQv

title:

Scientific models help researchers explain
title_en:
New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain and predict real-world systems—like how a single nerve cell fires, or what happens when neutron stars collide. Recent advances have transformed how scientists fit complex models to data. But scientists still typically write the models manually, and usually need to weigh up several competing versions, each of which might explain the data in a different way.

In a guest post, Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl describe how AI is starting to help with these parts of the process. By writing, running, fitting, and revising scientific models as code, AI can explore many possible model structures, and find out which explanations the data support.

title_en:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

RT @GoogleAI: Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and e
title_en:
RT @GoogleAI: Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and editing limit up to 15 seconds, and made updates to how scenes hold together over time. We've also given character speech an upgrade, reduced visual glitches like jump cuts, and made sure the model stays even truer to any reference assets you upload.

So… what does all of that actually mean for you?

It gives you more room to tell your story. With up to 15 seconds to work with, you have more flexibility to create what you need — videos look more cinematic and smooth, offering stronger consistency that keeps objects anchored from start to finish. And when characters speak, the dialogue sounds more fluid and natural.

Forcing the internal dynamics to be linear is overly restrictive, IMHO.

title:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records ca
title_en:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records can ruin lives.

GenLayer aims to settle AI-agent disputes in minutes: one AI validator proposes a verdict, others check independently, and decisions can be appealed.

On 27 March 2023, Alison MacPherson paid via RingGo on Hunter Street in Kirkcaldy. She typed 9 for 8 and missed the Z. A penalty followed.

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

AI can't rewrite laws or guarantee truth. Millions of agent deals need evidence checked and decisions open to challenge.

If an AI agent pays under the wrong ID, what matters more: the receipt, the intent or the rule?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_en:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records can ruin lives.

GenLayer aims to settle AI-agent disputes in minutes: one AI validator proposes a verdict, others check independently, and decisions can be appealed.

On 27 March 2023, Alison MacPherson paid via RingGo on Hunter Street in Kirkcaldy. She typed 9 for 8 and missed the Z. A penalty followed.

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

AI can't rewrite laws or guarantee truth. Millions of agent deals need evidence checked and decisions open to challenge.

If an AI agent pays under the wrong ID, what matters more: the receipt, the intent or the rule?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_zh:
她付了停车费。错误的数字和缺失的 Z 将她送上了法庭。

@GenLayer 的电影给我的震撼是：不良记录会毁掉生活。

GenLayer 的目标是在几分钟内解决人工智能代理纠纷：一名人工智能验证者提出裁决，其他人独立检查，并且可以对决定提出上诉。

2023 年 3 月 27 日，Alison MacPherson 在柯科迪亨特街通过 RingGo 付款。她8投9中，但没有击中Z。随后受到了处罚。

她的收据与时间和地点相符。法庭支持她。法伊夫议会提出上诉。 2024 年 1 月 8 日，上级法庭推翻了该判决并将其发回。

法官接受了她的诚意，但付款涵盖了另一辆车。

付款是真实的。登记不是她的。

李·卡斯尔顿 (Lee Castleton) 在影片中面临着更糟糕的情况：地平线错误地显示了 23,000 英镑的差距。在没有律师的情况下，他面临 321,000 英镑的法律费用和破产。

人工智能无法重写法律或保证真相。数以百万计的代理交易需要检查证据，决策也需要接受质疑。

如果人工智能代理使用错误的 ID 付款，收据、意图还是规则哪个更重要？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

title:

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people t
title_en:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.
title_zh:
人们应该始终掌控未来。

OpenAI 反对这样一种观念，即人们被降级到做“人工智能系统认为对人类有意义的奖励”的事情是可以接受的。

人们不应该将对未来的控制权交给超级智能，而这一要求最终应该限制人工智能的进步。

title_en: Google says its education updates give schools "more choice, not less"; Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default and can be enabled individually (@newsfromgoogle)
title_zh: 谷歌回应教育版AI更新：默认关闭
author: @newsfromgoogle
author_role: AI 先锋观察者
summary_en: Google announced that its education updates, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and AI Search, will be turned off by default, allowing schools to enable them individually. This move aims to address growing concerns from educators regarding student data privacy and classroom control.
summary_zh: 谷歌针对教育界对AI工具的隐私与控制担忧，宣布旗下Gemini等AI功能在教育版中默认处于关闭状态。
full_text_zh: 谷歌表示，其教育更新为学校提供了“更多选择，而不是更少”； Gemini、Gemini Notebook 和搜索默认处于关闭状态，可以单独启用

title:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff
title_en:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff for streams, fliers, YT stuff, banners, logos, etc...  A few big ticket items, but lots of little projects.

It is hands down the most miserable, time wasting, and laborious processes I've ever experienced when it comes to dealing with contract work.  And I did contracts in heavy civil construction...

A few thousand pissed down the drain on referred artists that just ghosted me after taking deposits.

Thumbnail artists that think they know what is better on a thumbnail than I do, so they completely ignore directions and do their own thing...

Logos that are copy right infringements or such near copies of other work it's shameful.

1 in 5.  MAYBE.  That's how many acted like actual professionals, delivered work on time, did what was asked, and finished the work.  Almost all of those were corporate firms too, not individuals.

It's so bad I've mostly just avoided having to use the industry when ever possible.  But the next time a big project I need comes up I'm going to double book it.

I'll go the traditional route, and the AI route.  And that is what will decide how I spend my money, and more importantly my time, going forward.

The OP is right.  Artists aren't saving their own careers.  They are pushing people to other less shitty interactions, and have been for years.

The difference is, there was no other choice before.  There is now.

title:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesl
title_en:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesla’s Cortex 1 and Cortex 2 clusters at Giga Texas are already in production at well over 200 MW combined, with a stated target of ~400 MW of SI (Super Intelligence) training compute by the end of 2026.  That capacity is primarily for training vehicle autonomy/FSD and Optimus models, remember those? 
We are running an enormous fleet on FSD.  
The difference vs SpaceX/xAI is priority. xAI is a pure AI lab that needs massive generic training flops for frontier models (and can sell excess capacity to Anthropic and others). 
Tesla’s highest-value use of the same capital is our proprietary real-world data flywheel for cars and bots. 
Diverting significant capacity to external customers would slow the exact products that justify Tesla’s valuation premium today.  

2. Merchant GPU compute is a brutal business Tesla doesn’t need to enter Rapid GPU depreciation and stranded capacity risk are real (Elon has commented on half-built data centers and idle chips). 
Nvidia owns the silicon stack; hyperscalers and specialized neoclouds already dominate the rental market. 

Tesla’s actual competitive advantage in the AI infrastructure stack is energy, not training chips. It has already sold hundreds of millions to ~$1B of Megapacks into the Colossus buildouts. That’s higher-margin, more defensible, and leverages what Tesla already does at scale.⁠ 
Selling raw flops would put Tesla in direct competition with Nvidia, AWS, CoreWeave, etc., in a capital-intensive, fast-depreciating business where it has no structural edge.  

3. The Dojo experience is a cautionary tale Tesla shut down Dojo in 2025 after Elon called the Dojo 2 design an “evolutionary dead end” and much of the team left. The company pivoted hard to Nvidia for training clusters while focusing its own silicon (AI5/AI6 and later) on inference in vehicles and robots. Re-entering custom training hardware at scale just to become a merchant seller would repeat a hard lesson.⁠ 

However, all this chip know-how is not lost and used now in the Terafab pilot.  

4. SpaceX’s speed is real, but it’s solving a different problem Colossus 1  and 2 are impressive, and SpaceX’s construction/execution culture is a genuine advantage for pure data-center buildouts. 

Tesla’s construction teams are optimized for vehicle and energy product factories, not multi-gigawatt pure-play AI campuses. 

SpaceX/xAI also benefits from being able to treat excess capacity as a revenue stream; Tesla’s equivalent excess capacity is better used accelerating FSD and Optimus software.⁠  

5. On “build it and sell it to SpaceX” Tesla is already the power supplier to those clusters. 
The more logical path (if any) is modular hardware like the Megapod rather than competing head-on as a pure compute seller. Even then, SpaceX is currently the world’s fastest large-scale data-center builder. 

Tesla’s scarce capital and engineering bandwidth is better spent on the products only Tesla can ship  

So, to sum it up:  
Tesla is already scaling to 400 MW of training compute for its own FSD and Optimus needs. 
Merchant GPU rental is a low-moat, high-depreciation business that Nvidia and the hyperscalers already own. 
Tesla’s real AI infrastructure edge is energy and the proprietary physical-world data only its fleet generates. 
Selling flops to SpaceX or anyone else would just slow the higher-value autonomy and robotics timeline.

full_text_zh:
这会比平常长一点：

1.特斯拉正在构建计算，只是为了我们自己的最高投资回报率用例特斯拉位于德克萨斯州 Giga 的 Cortex 1 和 Cortex 2 集群已经投入生产，总功率远超 200 MW，其既定目标是到 2026 年底实现约 400 MW 的 SI（超级智能）训练计算。该能力主要用于训练车辆自动驾驶/FSD 和 Optimus 模型，还记得那些吗？
我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。

summary_zh:
400 MW 的 SI（超级智能）训练计算。该能力主要用于训练车辆自动驾驶/FSD 和 Optimus 模型，还记得那些吗？
我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。
